# Vendored icons — Lucide (ISC)

A curated **41-icon subset** of [Lucide](https://lucide.dev), stored as SVG path
data in `lucide_icons.hpp` and regenerated by `tools/gen_icons.py`. Full license
in `LICENSE-lucide.txt`. Per the "vendor, don't depend" rule these are checked
in, not fetched at runtime or from a CDN.

## Why path data and not an icon font

The GUI already ships **Font Awesome as a TTF** (`../fonts/fa-solid-900.ttf`),
which is the right shape for ImGui — one glyph, one draw call, no DOM.

It is the wrong shape for a website, for three separate reasons:

- an icon font is a **blocking download**, so the page paints without its icons;
- when it fails it renders as a **box or a missing glyph**, not as nothing;
- it is **invisible to a screen reader**, or worse, read out as a private-use
  codepoint.

Inline SVG has none of those problems: it inherits `currentColor` (so the
theme's computed contrast applies to icons for free, with no second palette to
keep in sync), scales with the type because it is sized in `em`, costs no
request, and carries `aria-hidden` beside its own visible label.

And the reason that decides it for this project specifically: **a deployed
Hormiga site reaches no CDN.** An icon served from somebody else's network is an
icon that disappears when they turn it off — the same argument that vendored the
webfonts.

## Why only the web

Icons are emitted into the **website** domain and deliberately not into email:
Gmail strips inline SVG. An icon that renders as nothing in the client most of an
organization's readers use is worse than the text separator it replaced. See
`okf/concepts/blocks-and-domains.md`.

## Adding an icon

Fetch it from the Lucide repository into a folder of `.svg` files and re-run:

    python tools/gen_icons.py <folder-of-svgs>

The generator keeps only the inner markup — every Lucide icon shares the same
`<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" …>` wrapper, which the renderer
emits once.
